tasks.description: Self-healing ingest: heal_blank_frames() recovers NaN rows from PNGs on every preprocess run
Georeference correction: replace the 480x480-derived crop with the true NEA bounds and ingest the native 217x120 domain
tasks.notes: WORSE THAN TRACKED: the crop was not merely miscalibrated. On a 120x217 image the guard clamped rows 80:270 -> 80:120 and cols 130:350 -> 130:217, keeping the BOTTOM-RIGHT CORNER (rows 67-100%, cols 60-100%) and bilinear-upsampling 40x87 -> 190x220; the lat/lon coords (1.0-1.6N, 103.5-104.1E) were fiction. Fixed: full native domain, no crop, no resample. Bounds lat 1.1450-1.4572, lon 103.565-104.130 from weather.gov.sg page source, corroborated by cheeaun/checkweather-sg; cross-check 0.002602 deg/px lat vs 0.002604 lon = square pixels ~0.29 km, matching the NEA product spec. PHYSICAL VALIDATION (the acceptance gate, per L009): rain within ~1.5 km of geocoded flood cells at event time went from 19% of events (median peak 0.00 mm/hr) to 100% (median peak 51.57 mm/hr). This also resolves the residual half of L008 — flood cells read 0 mm/hr because of this crop, not because FLOOD_RISK warnings precede rain.

tasks.description: Alpha-aware colour conversion + exact-match 33-colour NEA LUT (replaces nearest-RGB against 11 anchors)
tasks.notes: ORIGINAL PREMISE DISPROVED: alpha is binary (0/255) archive-wide and transparent RGB is always (0,0,0), which already mapped to 0 mm/hr — dropping alpha was harmless, and these PNGs carry no basemap (they are pure overlays). The real source of the 'phantom drizzle <=~4 mm/hr floor' was BILINEAR RESAMPLING of a banded field: upsampling turned 9 discrete values into 7,302 and pushed nonzero cells from 68.5% to 95.8% on a rainy frame. Removed with the resize. THIRD DEFECT FOUND: nearest-RGB matching against 11 anchors while NEA uses exactly 33 discrete colours produced 8/33 NON-MONOTONIC mappings (lightest teal -> 2.0 mm/hr while 5 brighter cyans -> 1.0; magenta 255,0,255 -> 80 while a lighter magenta -> 100). Replaced with an exact-match LUT over all 33 colours; unknown colours are counted and reported, never snapped. Ramp ordering derived from the archive by three agreeing methods (distance-transform depth, spatial-adjacency graph walk, RGB continuity); absolute values log-uniform 0.5-100 mm/hr = 0.719 dBR/band, justified by the product being dBR. 0 opaque pixels archive-wide fall outside the ramp. Alpha now masked explicitly regardless.

stages.name: Diffusion Nowcaster Training
stages.notes:
UNBLOCKED 2026-09-22. The old blocker ('until Stage 3 reaches 90-day archive, ~late August 2026') had been satisfied for ~1 month unnoticed - archive hit 90d on ~2026-08-20 and is now 123d. See lessons L013.
REAL RUN LAUNCHED 2026-09-22 ~20:50 SGT: 300,000 steps, batch 4, num_workers 0. Measured throughput 132 ms/step (7.56 steps/s) on RTX 4060 8GB -> ~11h wall clock. 48,192 train / 3,249 val samples, 25.8M params. Checkpoints every 1,000 steps to checkpoints/nowcaster/; --resume auto works, so the run survives a travel shutdown.
FIX 2026-09-22: default num_workers 2 -> 0. RadarDataset holds the whole archive in RAM (3.45 GB at 33k frames) and Windows spawn cannot pickle it to workers - it crashed with OSError 22 / truncated pickle. Worked in June only because the archive was 1.21 GB. num_workers>0 now raises with the real reason. Proper fix (lazy/memmap reads in RadarDataset) still open - see docs/history/spike_nowcast_today.md PRODUCTION DELTA.
Today's 22-Sep flash floods land at index 33,058 -> TEST split (starts 2026-09-10 23:50), so they are a clean holdout; 139 usable test samples dated 22 Sep, contiguity OK only because of the backfill above.
RUN 1 FAILED (2026-09-22, steps 0-17,000): fp16 GradScaler collapse. Scale ratcheted one-way 2**19 -> 3.8e-37; learning stopped by ~step 12,000 and steps 15/16/17k score an identical val_loss 0.06826 vs 0.01467 at step 10,000 (60 fixed val batches, identical noise, bf16). Weights stayed finite throughout because the scaler skipped the bad steps, which is why it hid. See lessons L016.
RUN 2 IN PROGRESS (2026-09-23 09:01 SGT): resumed from ckpt_step_10000 in bf16, no GradScaler, 300k steps. Healthy at step 10,600 (loss 0.013-0.019, zero nan). Dead fp16 checkpoints quarantined in checkpoints/nowcaster/dead_fp16_run/.
Also fixed: val now aggregates finite batches only (sum()/len() turned 1 bad batch of ~800 into a NaN epoch, destroying the signal that would have caught this at step 15,000); checkpoint retention 5k milestones + 3 recent (~93 GB -> ~18 GB); find_latest_checkpoint + pruning rank by mtime so a rollback isn't undone by higher-numbered abandoned checkpoints.
RUN 2 was reaped twice for host memory pressure (steps 44,000 and earlier), not a training fault. ROOT CAUSE of the footprint found 2026-09-23: RadarDataset held the archive as float32 (3.46 GB) AND train.py built train+val datasets that each loaded their own full copy -- 6.93 GB, essentially the whole ~7 GB process. Fixed by uint8 codebook storage (the product is banded: exactly 34 distinct values archive-wide, so this is lossless) plus one shared copy per process. Dataset RSS 6.93 -> 0.92 GB; process ~7.0 -> ~2.6 GB; no throughput cost (129 vs 132 ms/step); startup halved. Verified bit-exact against the old path (tasks/repro/codebook_dataset_repro.py, 11/11) so the run could resume without its inputs shifting.
RUN 3 IN PROGRESS (2026-09-23 11:09 SGT): resumed from ckpt_step_44000. Val progression so far 0.0121 (15k) -> 0.0102 (20k) -> 0.0098 (30k) -> 0.0096 (40k), zero nan.
OPEN: radar_stats.json is stale (n_samples 21,005 vs 33,246; log_mean 0.0279 vs current 0.0287). Deliberately NOT regenerated -- it would shift normalisation under the resumed run. Decide at the next clean-start run.
RUN 6 COMPLETE 2026-09-25 05:57 (v-prediction, full frames, alpha=0): 300k steps, guard passed (1 degenerate validation at 10k, then 58 clean) -> stage4_complete.flag earned. Realistic rain statistics (wet 1.80% vs observed 1.86% @2mm/hr) but weak placement.

tasks.description: NaN-aware sample filtering in RadarDataset (exclude windows containing blank all-NaN frames)
tasks.notes: 862 blank frames archive-wide sit at valid timestamps, so they passed the 4.7 contiguity filter; 896 NaN-poisoned samples reached the splits (train 659, val 130, test 107). Fix: frame-validity mask (any-NaN = blank; archive is perfectly bimodal, 0 partial-NaN frames) + cumsum window check over the full sample span, symmetric with the gap filter; compute_stats made nan-safe (nanmean/nanstd/nanmax). Existing radar_stats.json (Jun 5, pre-blanks) deliberately left untouched to keep normalisation constants stable. Post-fix repro (tasks/repro/nan_samples_repro.py): 0 NaN samples in all splits; drops train 667/val 130/test 109.

stages.name: Evaluation & Flash Flood Map
stages.notes:
Ground-truth pipeline live: collect_flood_labels.py (Telegram, daily 09:00 SGT scheduled task, conda env) -> flood_labels.parquet; build_flood_eval_dataset.py cross-references labels to radar.zarr -> flood_eval_dataset.parquet. CRITICAL FIX 2026-07-10: '[HH:MM hours]' tags in PUB messages are SGT wall-clock but were stored as UTC — every label was 8h late and all geocoded flood cells read 0.0 mm/hr (see lessons L009; supersedes the L007/L008 'verified' claim). Collector now parses SGT -> UTC (nearest-day resolution); parquet rebuilt from raw messages.json. Rebuilt eval dataset 2026-07-10: 34 labels through 2026-07-08 (23 RAIN_WARNING, 11 FLOOD_RISK, 0 FLASH_FLOOD), 31/34 radar-matched (11/11 flood events), rain now visible at geocoded cells (e.g. Jalan Boon Lay 4.7 mm/hr near-cell at warning minute). Geocode cache: all 10 strings resolved — KPE slip-road hand-fixed 2026-07-10 to the Buangkok East Drive junction (1.3775, 103.9090, cell 70,149); all 11 flood events now carry spatial cells. FULLY AUTOMATED 2026-07-10: 'SG-Weather Telegram Labels' task (daily 09:00 SGT, conda env) now chains collect -> geocode (cache/gazetteer first, OneMap failures degrade to unresolved without breaking the chain) -> build_flood_eval_dataset; ExecutionTimeLimit raised PT10M -> PT20M; chain verified end-to-end (exit 0, parquets refreshed). evaluation_report.json (2026-06-18) is a smoke-run placeholder — not a real result. NOT yet wired into evaluate.py (would change Stage 5 semantics; awaiting approval). Audit 2026-07-18: label chain healthy end-to-end (daily runs exit 0, state.json last_run current); still 34 labels, none since Jul 8 — verified against the live PUB channel web preview that the channel itself has been quiet (newest post matches our last stored message), collector not at fault. Notable: radar showed large heavy-rain footprints Jul 10/12/16 with no PUB heavy-rain advisory — channel may only post a subset of NEA warnings.
UPDATE 2026-09-22: FIRST REAL FLASH_FLOOD EVENTS since collection began - King's Road (issued 17:11 SGT, subsided 17:37) and Coronation Road (17:15, subsided 17:28), both Bukit Timah/Coronation. Radar confirms a real convective cell: 71.8 mm/hr at the flood cell 16:30-16:50, collapsing to 8.3 by 17:35 as the squall advected E; the 16:00-18:00 window exceeded 99.98% of all archive frames by area>=60mm/hr. Eval dataset rebuilt after the backfill: matched flood events 46/48 -> 48/48 (see L014). 3 labels remain permanently unmatched (2026-05-24 06:40, 2026-06-29 18:15/19:30 UTC) - radar older than NEA retention.
EVAL 2026-09-25 (FSS @2 mm/hr, lead is 35 min from last observed frame; pixel = 0.29 km, NOT 1 km): model 0.158 vs persistence 0.451 at 11.9 km -> FAIL. Model uses its context (true 0.095 vs shuffled 0.039) but weakly. Residual forecasting probe: worse (0.091), reverted. Optical flow: Farneback 0.406, and even ORACLE true-displacement shift loses to persistence (0.337 vs 0.384 interior) -> at this scale rain grows/decays more than it moves. Persistence skill vs lead @12 km: 0.708 (5m) / 0.406 (35m) / 0.313 (60m) / 0.246 (90m); below the 'useful' line (~0.52) from ~20 min, so it is beatable in principle. Next source of skill must be convective initiation/decay: time-of-day, longer history, or large-scale environment (ERA5). See docs/history/spike_optical_flow.md.
CRITERION AMENDED + PRIMARY PASSED 2026-09-25: CRPS skill vs persistence +0.437, 95% CI [+0.338, +0.557] (300k model, 200 test samples x 8 members). Pooled ensemble FSS at 2 mm/hr ties persistence (0.820 vs 0.801); heavy rain (>=10 mm/hr) is the open target (0.530 vs 0.612). Remaining Stage 5 items: 60/90-min leads, case-study notebook, flood-risk overlay notebook, <5 min inference. CLOSED 2026-09-27: all deliverables met; heavy-rain target closed as a documented radar-only limitation by user decision.
